meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
You're telling me one line. Show me the page it's on, Hale. And is that everything you have, or is there more?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire's case is something the principal will hear about from me today. Now, the page with that line on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me you should have called me before entering the zero and that you were sorry, and nothing else was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, my questions about who decided and whether Owen was heard first answered, and the page with that quotation sent to me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed beyond your apology for not calling first.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry." It owned the process failure in two sentences and got a flat "Okay."
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family." Bringing up Claire sent her cold and put the principal back on the table.
Try next time: after the apology, answer her question about who decided and whether Owen was spoken to, and have the essay page with the quoted line ready to turn toward her before she asks for it.
